_source: docs/design/12-ui-ux.md §8 (Draft v1, report 98 amendments C-25/C-35/C-59/C-62/C-63/C-64/C-65/C-71/C-72/G-8). Transcribed verbatim; no number invented here.
_units: Every length is dp (Android density-independent pixels, doc 12 §2.1) unless the key says _m (metres) or _s / _ms (time).

layout._top_bar_max_rows: §2.4's collapse solver hides P5-P7 once demotion runs out. On a near-square display (Fold inner, 2160x1856) the four never-hidden chips plus a measured value string still overflow one 48 dp row, and A1/A2 forbid clipping — so the bar wraps to a second row BEFORE anything is hidden. 1 restores the doc's single-row behaviour exactly.

_comment_states: Exactly four data states — these four ARE doc 11's 2-bit overlay_state (C-64). SELECTED is not one of them.

overlay._enabled_modes: An overlay ships enabled only once the sim behind it publishes an OverlayQuery (doc 12 §4.4). POWER is live (doc 04); WATER/POLICE/FIRE/TRAFFIC stay listed, greyed and tooltip-explained (A14: every blocked action states its reason in words) until docs 05/06/10 land — never hidden, so the player learns the shape of the console once.
overlay._shader_global: doc 11 reads the active overlay from this project shader global; its value is the mode's INDEX INTO overlay.modes above (none 0, power 1, water 2, police 3, fire 4, traffic 5). The int is written by ui/overlay_rail.gd and by nothing else; the per-instance 2-bit overlay_state that the building shader tints with is doc 11's and is never set from here (C-64).

alerts._comment: The §2.15 alerts centre: the persistent feed behind the banner stack. Class and surface come from in_app_alerts above (C-71/C-72) — this block only says which sim event becomes which notification, and it is a STAND-IN for doc 08's data/notifications.json event->class map. When that file lands it REPLACES `events` wholesale; the two are never merged.

incident_drawer._comment: S6 (doc 12 §2.6). The drawer's GEOMETRY is already in `layout` (drawer_w_ratio/min/max, drawer_row_h_dp, drawer_handle_dp, drawer_handle_center_from_bottom_dp, drawer_anim_s) and its escalation-bar thresholds are already in `thresholds` (escalation_bar_critical_remaining_tiers, escalation_bar_held_when_assist_ratio_ge) — this block adds only what §2.6 says and no other block does: the sort orders, the row cap, and the two glyph sets.
incident_drawer._max_rows: The drawer is a list of things to DO, not a log; doc 06's storm cascade can open dozens at once and a list past this depth is not readable on a phone. The lowest-tier row is the one dropped, never a T5.
incident_drawer._tier_glyphs: §2.6's A5 redundancy set, verbatim: T1 ▪, T2 ▴, T3 ▴▴, T4 ◆, T5 ✶. The tier DIGIT is the primary channel; these reinforce it. Colours are palette.tier1…tier5, which already exist.
incident_drawer._kind_glyphs: One per doc 06 incident `type`. Keys are doc 06's type ids verbatim so a rename there is a visible miss here rather than a silent fallback.

unit_picker._comment: S7 (doc 12 §2.6 steps 1-5). Sheet height and row height are `layout.unit_picker_h_dp` / `layout.unit_row_h_dp`; the rank key is §2.6's and lives in ui/unit_picker_model.gd. This block carries only the department glyph set — doc 06 owns the department names.

dashboard._comment: S8 (doc 12 §2.10). §2.10 specifies four tabs; `tabs` lists the ones whose sim queries exist. Infrastructure needs per-feeder headroom (doc 04) and per-zone pressure (doc 05); Response needs the unit roster with rolling response times (doc 06). Adding either is an edit to this array plus its rows, never a code change.
dashboard._series: What ui/history_model.gd rings. `power01`/`water01` are the [0,1] service fractions the ⚡/💧 chips read, sampled at the same hourly boundary as the rest.
dashboard._history_capacity: 168 hourly samples = 7 game-days, exactly what §2.10's '7-day treasury chart' needs. The ring is fixed-size and is NOT persisted: doc 12 §3.2 fixes the `ui` save section and report 98 §E2 makes save identity exact.

budget._comment: The Economy tab's ledger. Keys are doc 03's settle-snapshot keys VERBATIM (`revenue.*` and `expenses.*` from EconomySystem.settle_hour) so a rename there shows up as a missing line here rather than as a wrong total. Order is the reading order, not doc 03's; the tax ladder itself is doc 03's and is never restated here.

settings._comment: S9 (doc 12 §2.13), Phase-1 pages only. Every row is data so the sheet holds no option list and no default; `options_from`/`default_from` resolve against data/render.json (doc 11 owns the graphics presets) and this file's own `defaults` block.

rows._comment: S12's reset (doc 12 §2.17: the tutorial never shows again once done, unless the player asks for it here). Switching it ON restarts the coach flow from step 0 and the row switches itself back OFF — it is a door, not a preference, and it is per-city, so it is NOT in device_scoped_keys.

save_slots._comment: S0/S9 Data & Saves. game/save_service.gd owns the files and the meta shape {slot, saved_at_unix, day_index, population, treasury}; this block owns only how many slots the player sees and which one autosave owns.

pause_menu._comment: Single-scene game: QUIT saves first and then closes the app, so `quit` is an intent the shell fulfils, never a bare get_tree().quit() from a view.

camera._comment: Interaction range only (C-63). Projection constants fov_deg/near_m/far_m live in data/render.json (doc 11) and are read from there; they must never be added to this block.

onboarding._comment: S12 (doc 12 §2.17) at the scope the shipped verbs support. The doc's eleven-step table assumes player-drawn power lines and water mains, a Land tab and a review-ledger beat; §2.17's own thesis sentence — 'one component fails, four other systems degrade, the player dispatches a finite crew, and the lights come back on' — is what this table teaches with the commands that exist today (cmd_place_building, cmd_place_grid_component, cmd_dispatch_unit, trigger_tutorial_transformer_failure). Steps the verbs cannot carry yet (confirm_water, review_ledger, service_building, upgrade, buy_land) are NOT renumbered or faked: they are absent, and adding one is a row here plus its string, never a code change.
onboarding._geometry: §2.17's coach-mark rendering, verbatim: dim #000000 @ 0.55, an 8 dp / 12 dp rounded cutout animated over layout.coach_cutout_anim_s, a bubble no wider than 240 dp, and copy capped at 90 characters so it reads in one glance.
onboarding._director: §2.17's global guarantee: the disaster director is suppressed for the whole tutorial and 300 real seconds after it, so the only incident that exists is the scripted one. The model REQUESTS both through its action queue; doc 07 owns the switch.
onboarding._region_radius: How much slack a `region` match allows, in tiles (Chebyshev). 1 keeps the marked lot the marked lot while forgiving a fat finger on the tile next to it.
onboarding._camera: Step 1 completes on observed CameraState movement — both verbs, because a player who only pans has not learnt to zoom. 48 m is six tiles; 0.05 zoom_t is a quarter of one double-tap step.

steps._advance_note: No `match` on the incident kind, on purpose: SimEventBus.emit stamps `type` with the EVENT name, so a bus event never carries doc 06's incident type. It does not need to — §2.17's global guarantee is that the director is suppressed and RNG spawning is off for the whole tutorial, so the only incident that can be created here is the scripted one.

in_app_alerts._comment: FOREGROUND banners and toasts ONLY (C-71/C-72). These are ~3x doc 08's PUSH budgets in data/notifications.json and that is deliberate: an in-app banner costs a glance the player is already giving. Never read these to decide a push, or a push budget to decide a banner.
